page.layout: One column of text. Above it, a full-width dedication heading in capitals with the greeting "S. P. D." beneath. In the text block at the left, beside the opening lines, a woodcut vignette (an emblem with a figure, no printed text). No running head, page number, or margin notes.

main_text.head: GVILIELMVS XYLANDER Augustanus, ALBERTO A STETEN, Georgij V.C.F. adolescenti optimę indolis atque spei,
main_text.p: Vos ad te, ALBERTE carissime, mitto Libellos, eos Graecos ex vetustissimis membranis, rarissimo, mihi, aliàs nunquam viso literarum genere conscriptis, liberali permissu Illustrissimi optimi{3} PRINCIPIS ac Domini mei, in cuius bibliotheca is codex abs me erat repertus, transcriptos, superiore anno, cum otiosus Augustae essem, in Latinum sermonem transtuli. De quibus edendis in lucem cum cogitarem, simul venit mihi in mentem M. Antonini de vita sua librorum, quos (quanquam εὐλογίας[?] potius operis, quam ipsum opus, ipsosq; integros libros esse iudico) ante annos fere novem à me Latinos factos ad patrem tuum, virum omni vera laude cumulatissimum, officij causa emiseram. page.notes: The woodcut vignette at the left of the opening lines is an illustration with no text; it is not transcribed. Faint show-through of the reverse page and a handwritten or stamped mark at the top right are excluded. The "S. P. D." greeting is set as a paragraph, not a heading. The mark after "optimi" and the mark after "ipsosq" are printed abbreviation or reference signs, copied as seen; their exact form is uncertain. The Greek word "εὐλογίας" is read from a small image and is doubtful. The signature at the foot is hard to read and is marked [?]. The word "cofcriptis" is read as "conscriptis" with the long s written as a plain s; the reading is doubtful.
